title: A filtered colimit of smooth algebras is a filtered colimit of standard smooth algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra which is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Then $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of standard smooth $R$-algebras: there are a small filtered category $\mathcal K$ ($\mathcal K$ has at least one object, any two objects of $\mathcal K$ map to a common object, and any two parallel arrows $a,b:k\to k'$ are equalized by some arrow $c:k'\to k''$, $c\circ a=c\circ b$), a functor $k\mapsto C_k$ from $\mathcal K$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras (transition maps homomorphisms of $R$-algebras) such that every $C_k$ is a standard smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\iota_k:C_k\to\Lambda$ such that $(\Lambda,(\iota_k)_{k\in\mathcal K})$ is a colimit of the diagram $k\mapsto C_k$ in the category of commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CI (lemma-colimit-standard-smooth, line 675) with its proof (lines 681-691: Algebra Lemma Tag 07C3 lemma-when-colimit and Lemma Tag 07CH lemma-smooth-standard-smooth)

proof.text: *Step 1 (a set of standard smooth algebras).* Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of all $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with $n\ge c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ such that the class of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ is a unit of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ (a set: it is indexed by the tuples $(n,c,f_1,\dots,f_c)$). Every member of $\mathcal E$ is standard smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] (the identity is a standard smooth presentation) and of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] (the same quotient is a presentation). Conversely, if $C$ is a standard smooth $R$-algebra with standard smooth presentation $\alpha:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}C$, then the image of $g=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ in $C$ is a unit, hence (applying the ring isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}$) so is the class of $g$ in $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$; so $E:=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\in\mathcal E$ and $\alpha:E\to C$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras. Thus every standard smooth $R$-algebra is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a member of $\mathcal E$.

proof.text: *Step 2 (factoring through a smooth stage).* By hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras] there are a small filtered category $J$, a functor $j\mapsto B_j$ from $J$ to commutative $R$-algebras with every $B_j$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $R$-algebra maps $\iota_j:B_j\to\Lambda$ such that $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$ is a colimit in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1), $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings. Now let $A$ be an $R$-algebra of finite presentation and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Choose a presentation, an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi:C_0:=R[y_1,\dots,y_p]/(h_1,\dots,h_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] (Algebra 00QO, the direction (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of 07C3) applied to the diagram $j\mapsto B_j$, the colimit $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$, $C_0$ and $g=\alpha\circ\varphi$, there are $j\in J$ and an $R$-algebra map $g':C_0\to B_j$ with $\iota_j\circ g'=\alpha\circ\varphi$. Put $\beta:=g'\circ\varphi^{-1}:A\to B_j$; then $\iota_j\circ\beta=\alpha$, a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}B_j\xrightarrow{\iota_j}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by $R$-algebra maps with $B_j$ smooth over $R$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CI (lemma-colimit-standard-smooth, lines 681-691): 'we know we can factor it as A -> B -> Lambda with B smooth over R' (Algebra 07C3 (1)=>(2), i.e. 00QO)

proof.text: *Step 3 (factoring through a member of $\mathcal E$).* With $A,\alpha,j,\beta$ as in Step 2: $B_j$ is a smooth $R$-algebra, so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-standard-smooth] (Smoothing 07CH) there are a standard smooth $R$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] and $R$-algebra maps $\sigma:B_j\to C$, $\rho:C\to B_j$ with $\rho\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{B_j}$ (the further assertion of that node, that $C$ is smooth over $B_j$, is not used). By Step 1 choose $E\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:E\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. Put $\beta':=\theta^{-1}\circ\sigma\circ\beta:A\to E$ and $\gamma:=\iota_j\circ\rho\circ\theta:E\to\Lambda$, homomorphisms of $R$-algebras. Then $\gamma\circ\beta'=\iota_j\circ\rho\circ\sigma\circ\beta=\iota_j\circ\beta=\alpha$. So every $R$-algebra map $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ with $A$ of finite presentation over $R$ factors as $A\xrightarrow{\beta'}E\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ with $E\in\mathcal E$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CI (lemma-colimit-standard-smooth, lines 681-691): 'Choose an R-algebra map B -> C with a retraction C -> B such that C is standard smooth over R, see Lemma 07CH. Then the desired factorization is A -> B -> C -> B -> Lambda'

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion by the criterion 07C3).* $\mathcal E$ is a set of commutative $R$-algebras each of finite presentation over $R$ (Step 1), and by Step 3 every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $A\to\Lambda$ with $A$ of finite presentation factors through a member of $\mathcal E$ by $R$-algebra maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit] (Algebra 07C3, (2)$\Rightarrow$(1)) there are a small filtered category $\mathcal K$ (filtered as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: nonempty, any two objects map to a common object, parallel arrows are equalized), a functor $k\mapsto C_k$ from $\mathcal K$ to commutative $R$-algebras with every $C_k\in\mathcal E$, and $R$-algebra maps $\iota_k:C_k\to\Lambda$ such that $(\Lambda,(\iota_k)_{k\in\mathcal K})$ is a colimit of this diagram in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Every $C_k\in\mathcal E$ is standard smooth over $R$ (Step 1) [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. This is the assertion.
